about: Netflix is the world's largest subscription video streaming service, with over 300 million paying members in more than 190 countries, offering original series and films (Stranger Things, Squid Game), licensed content, live events and games, and an advertising tier. Revenue near 45 billion dollars. Headquartered in Los Gatos, California; founded 1997. Listed on Nasdaq (NFLX). Global household brand, and a partner of major live sports such as boxing, NFL Christmas games and the Formula 1 Drive to Survive series.

Bilibili is a Chinese online video and entertainment platform popular with young users, offering user-generated videos, anime, games, live streaming and e-commerce. Earns from mobile games, advertising, premium memberships and value-added services, with about 100 million monthly users. Headquartered in Shanghai; founded 2009. Listed on Nasdaq (BILI) and in Hong Kong (9626). Strong Generation Z consumer brand in China, with partnerships in esports and sports.

Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment owns and operates the Toronto Maple Leafs (NHL), Toronto Raptors (NBA), Toronto FC (MLS) and Toronto Argonauts (CFL), and venues Scotiabank Arena and BMO Field. Earns from tickets, sponsorship, media rights and hospitality. Headquartered in Toronto. Owned by Bell and Rogers, which each hold 37.5 percent, with Larry Tanenbaum holding the remaining stake. A leading Canadian sports brand with strong fan base and existing sponsorship business.

Apple is a Cupertino, California technology company that designs iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods, Apple TV and Vision Pro, runs the App Store, and sells services such as iCloud, Apple Music, Apple TV+, Apple Pay and AppleCare. It sells to consumers and businesses worldwide through its own stores, online and carriers, with annual revenue near $400bn and about 160,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (AAPL) and among the world's most valuable companies. Among the most recognised consumer brands; F1 US broadcast rights from 2026, and a major marketing partner.

Concord Music Group is a Nashville-based music company covering recorded music, music publishing, theatricals and live production, with a catalogue spanning jazz, classic rock, Broadway and pop. Its labels include Fantasy, Stax, Concord Records and Rounder, and Concord Theatricals holds the rights to shows such as Rodgers and Hammerstein works. It earns royalties from streaming, licensing and live shows. Owned by Genstar Capital, GIC and Concord management, among others. Private. Brand known to the music industry; low consumer awareness.

DAZN is a London-based global sports streaming service, offering live and on-demand football, boxing, MMA, NFL, tennis and other sports to subscribers in over 200 markets, plus the Eleven and Foxtel acquisitions. It earns subscription fees and advertising, with annual revenue about GBP 3bn and tens of millions of viewers. Owned by Access Industries, led by Len Blavatnik. Private. A major consumer sports brand holding rights such as the FIFA Club World Cup 2025, and a sponsor of sports properties.

Flutter Entertainment is the world's largest online sports betting and gaming operator, with a UK registered office in Leeds and primary listing moved to the NYSE (FLUT). Brands include FanDuel, Paddy Power, Sky Bet, Betfair, PokerStars, Sportsbet and Junglee, serving tens of millions of customers in the US, UK, Ireland, Australia, Italy and India. Revenue is around $17bn. High consumer awareness and a heavy sports marketer, including league partnerships; F1 sponsor profile in betting is constrained by regulation in some markets.

Tencent Music Entertainment is a Shenzhen-based Chinese online music and audio group operating QQ Music, Kugou, Kuwo and WeSing karaoke, and Ximalaya audio platform. It earns subscription and social entertainment revenue from hundreds of millions of users, with revenue near RMB 30bn. Controlled by Tencent Holdings and listed on the NYSE (TME) and Hong Kong (1698). Very strong consumer brand in China, with limited recognition outside China.

BMG Music Publishing is the music publishing arm of BMG Rights Management, a Berlin-based music company (a Bertelsmann subsidiary, with KKR as co-owner until 2023) that manages publishing rights, recorded music and licensing for artists including Mick Jagger, Kylie Minogue and the Rolling Stones' catalog. Operates offices in over 20 markets, with a large catalog. Customers are songwriters, labels and media users. Known in the music industry, low direct consumer awareness.

Charter Communications is a Stamford, Connecticut-based US cable operator, offering Spectrum internet, mobile, TV and voice to about 57 million customers in 41 states, plus Spectrum Business, Spectrum Reach advertising and Spectrum News channels. Revenue is around $55 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (CHTR), and in 2025 it agreed to merge with Cox Communications. Very high consumer brand awareness in the US, and holder of sports media rights such as Lakers broadcasts via Spectrum SportsNet.

Rogers Communications is a Toronto-based Canadian telecom and media company, offering wireless, internet and cable to millions of customers, and owning the Toronto Blue Jays, Sportsnet, Rogers Centre and a stake in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment. It acquired Shaw in 2023. Listed on the TSX and NYSE (RCI). Controlled by the Rogers family. Very high consumer brand awareness in Canada and a major sports media and sponsorship player.

The Walt Disney Company is a Burbank, California-based entertainment conglomerate, founded in 1923, with studios (Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm, 20th Century), media networks (ABC, ESPN, National Geographic), streaming (Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+) and parks, experiences and products (Disney parks, cruise line, consumer products). Revenue is about $90 billion. Listed on NYSE (DIS). Among the most recognised consumer brands in the world, and a partner of F1 through ESPN and Star broadcast deals.

AMC Theatres is a Leawood, Kansas-based US movie theatre chain, the largest in the world, with about 900 theatres and 9,000 screens in the US and Europe (Odeon, UCI), owned by AMC Entertainment Holdings (NYSE: AMC). Revenue is about $4.6 billion from tickets and concessions. It became a meme stock in 2021. Chinese owner Wanda was its previous controlling shareholder. Very high consumer brand awareness in the US.

Comcast is a US media and technology conglomerate headquartered in Philadelphia and listed on Nasdaq (CMCSA). It owns Xfinity broadband and cable, NBCUniversal (NBC, Peacock, Universal Pictures, theme parks, Telemundo), Sky in Europe, and the Versant cable spin-off planned for 2026. It has over 30 million broadband customers and revenue near 120 billion dollars. Money comes from subscriptions, advertising, film and theme park admissions. Huge consumer brands and a major sports broadcaster, including NFL, Premier League and the Olympics, so a likely media partner.

Legendary Entertainment is a Burbank-based film, television and media company founded in 2000 by Thomas Tull and owned by China's Dalian Wanda Group since 2016. It produces and co-finances blockbusters such as Dune, Godzilla and Kong, the Jurassic World series (as financing partner), plus the Legendary Comics and television arms. Customers are studios, streamers and audiences; revenue comes from film, licensing and distribution. Strong entertainment brand with a track record of branded content partnerships.

Liberty Media is a US media and entertainment company based in Englewood, Colorado, controlled by chairman John Malone. It owns Formula One Group (Formula 1's commercial rights holder) and a Live Nation stake; the Braves baseball team (split off 2023) and SiriusXM (merged out 2024) no longer sit inside it. Listed on Nasdaq (FWONA/FWONK and others). Revenue is mainly F1 media rights, race promotion fees and sponsorship. Already central to F1.

Nexstar Media Group is the largest US local television station owner, headquartered in Irving, Texas and listed on Nasdaq (NXST), with over 200 stations reaching about 39 percent of US households, plus national cable network NewsNation and The CW. Revenue is around 5 billion dollars from retransmission fees and advertising, including political ads. Founded 1996. In 2025 it agreed to acquire Tegna. Audience-facing media company with large reach among US local viewers, relevant for advertising.

United Group is a multi-play telecoms and media provider in Southeast Europe, headquartered in Hoofddorp in the Netherlands and controlled by BC Partners. It operates mobile, broadband and pay-TV in Serbia (SBB), Bulgaria (Vivacom), Slovenia, Croatia, Montenegro and Bosnia, and owns N1 news and Nova TV channels plus sports rights. Millions of subscribers across the Balkans. Privately held, with debt-financed acquisitions. Strong regional consumer brand and sports broadcaster, so a potential media partner.

about: Universal Music Group is the world's largest music company, headquartered in Hilversum, Netherlands with major offices in Santa Monica and New York, and listed on Euronext Amsterdam (UMG). Its labels include Republic, Interscope, Island, Capitol, Def Jam and Deutsche Grammophon, with artists such as Taylor Swift, Drake and Billie Eilish, plus Universal Music Publishing and merchandise. Revenue is around 11 billion euros from streaming, licensing and live. Founded 1934 as Decca. Highly visible entertainment brand relevant to artist and music partnerships.

Cirsa is a Spanish gaming and leisure group headquartered in Terrassa, Catalonia, operating casinos, slot arcades, betting shops, bingo halls and online gaming in Spain, Italy, Latin America and Morocco, with revenue above 2 billion euros. Controlled by Blackstone since 2018 and listed on the Spanish stock exchange since 2025. Founded 1978 by the Lao family. Customers are casino and betting patrons. Strong gaming consumer brand in Spain, though advertising of gambling is restricted there.

SESAC Music Group is a US performing rights organisation and music licensing company, with offices in New York and Nashville, which collects royalties for songwriters, composers and publishers when their music is played on radio, TV, streaming and venues. It was acquired by Blackstone in 2017 and expanded through acquisitions including Harry Fox Agency and Rumblefish. Customers are music users and rights holders. Founded 1930. B2B music rights brand with limited public awareness.

Listed on Nasdaq (IQ). Very strong consumer brand in China, with a wide base of paying members.

Take-Two Interactive is a video game publisher and developer behind the Rockstar Games (Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption) and 2K labels (NBA 2K, WWE 2K, Borderlands, Civilization), plus Zynga mobile games acquired in 2022. Customers are gamers worldwide, with revenue of about $5.5 billion to $6 billion from game sales, in-game purchases and subscriptions. Headquartered in New York. Listed on Nasdaq (TTWO). Games are global consumer brands, with GTA among the best-selling franchises.

Create Music Group is a West Hollywood, California music services company providing distribution, rights management, publishing, royalty advances, and digital media and creator services for musicians, YouTube creators and labels. Revenue comes from distribution and licensing fees and advances. Crunchbase shows about $615 million in funding, mostly rights financing. Private. B2B and creator-facing brand, with some visibility in the digital music and creator communities.

about: Digikala is Iran's largest online retailer, selling electronics, fashion, books, home goods and groceries, with a marketplace for third-party sellers and Digipay payments. Headquartered in Tehran, founded in 2006 by brothers Hamid and Saeed Mohammadi. Customers are Iranian consumers. Funding is shown in Iranian rials. Because it operates in Iran, US and EU sanctions exposure makes it unsuitable for most international sponsorship. Very strong consumer brand domestically.

Cologix is a North American network-neutral data centre and interconnection operator, with facilities in markets such as Columbus, Dallas, Minneapolis, Montreal, Toronto and Vancouver, where enterprises, cloud providers and carriers connect and house equipment. Headquartered in Denver, Colorado. Revenue comes from colocation, interconnection and cloud connectivity fees. Owned by infrastructure investor Stonepeak. Crunchbase shows about $2.7 billion in funding, mainly financing. Private. B2B infrastructure brand with no consumer awareness.

New York holding company controlled by the Steinbrenner family that owns the New York Yankees baseball team, along with stakes in the YES Network and related real estate and hospitality ventures. Revenue comes from tickets, media rights, merchandise and sponsorship. The Yankees are one of the most valuable sports franchises in the world and a global consumer brand. The family-controlled company has a long history, and the team is based at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx.

London-listed gambling company Evoke PLC, formerly 888 Holdings, owner of William Hill, 888 Casino and Mr Green. HQ in the input shows Herzliya, Israel. Customers are UK and European bettors. Strong consumer brands in the UK, with sports betting sponsorship. Evoke is a large betting and gaming operator, with revenue of about GBP 1.7 billion. Its brands appear on sports shirts and advertising.

Gamma is a Los Angeles-based media and music company founded in 2021 by Larry Jackson, former head of Apple Music and Interscope Geffen, which backs artists and creators through a record label, publishing and film and television ventures. It raised about 1 billion dollars in a 2021 deal with Apple, Hollywood financiers and other backers. Customers are audiences streaming music, and Gamma earns revenue from recorded music, rights and content deals. Mid-level brand awareness, with artist signings such as Usher and Mary J. Blige adjacent partners; entertainment-sector fit.

Based in New York, with Endeavor as majority owner, and combined revenue of around 3 billion dollars or more. Large global fan base and heavy sponsorship activity, making it a peer sports property as well as a potential partner.

Headquartered in Wan Chai, Hong Kong; funding shown is around 5 billion Hong Kong dollars. Its prominence faded after the Evergrande group collapse. B2B and investment oriented with little consumer brand visibility.

about: Gray Media, formerly Gray Television, is a US broadcaster headquartered in Atlanta that owns and operates local television stations affiliated with CBS, NBC, ABC and Fox in over 100 US markets, reaching about 36 percent of households. It earns money from advertising, retransmission fees and political ads, and owns production studios in Atlanta. Listed on the NYSE (GTN), rebranded as Gray Media in 2025. Local news brands are well known in their markets, with regional sports coverage.
